final_candidates.decision_summary: Charge reversal on the exposed Sa-site loop (156-160) is a classic antibody-escape mechanism with minimal risk to folding or receptor binding.
Creates an N-linked glycosylation sequon (N158-S-S160) in the Sa site, enabling glycan shielding of a major epitope; head-region glycan additions are generally tolerated.
Surface charge reversal in the Sa-region (128-129) of early H1 strains likely disrupts antibody recognition while preserving structure and receptor-binding function.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence is available and the pool has converged after self-review; additional iteration is unlikely to change the Top-3.

history.rationale: Position 157 lies in the Sa antigenic site (156-160 loop) of WSN H1; charge-reversal at a surface-exposed epitope residue is a classic antibody-escape mechanism. The loop location makes folding disruption unlikely and it is adjacent to, not inside, the receptor-binding site.
Sa-site charge reversal on an exposed loop; strong escape rationale with minimal folding risk, remains top candidate.

S158N creates an N-X-S glycosylation sequon (N158-S159-S160) in the Sa site, potentially masking the epitope with a glycan — a well-documented immune-shielding strategy in H1 evolution. Some fitness cost from the added glycan is possible but head-region glycan additions are frequently tolerated.
Glycan-shielding mechanism in Sa site is a proven escape route; slight fitness uncertainty keeps it at rank 2.
Position 169 is in the Ca1/Sa-adjacent antigenic region (169-173) on the HA head; a Lys-to-Glu charge swap is expected to disrupt antibody binding while minimally affecting structure.
Kept in pool but tied slightly lower; Ca-region proximity introduces modest uncertainty versus pure Sa-site changes.

Position 188 sits in the Sb antigenic site (187-198); charge reversal here mimics natural escape substitutions. It borders the 190-helix receptor-binding region, so modest risk to receptor binding lowers confidence.
Sb-site escape is plausible, but adjacency to the 190-helix receptor-binding region caps confidence.
Residues 128-129 contribute to the Sa antigenic site in early H1 strains; E129K is a surface charge reversal likely to reduce antibody recognition with low structural risk.
Promoted above K169E: Sa-site charge reversal with lower structural risk than the Ca-adjacent K169E.
